/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 09 November 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2854 (49)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4459 (115)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2037 (34)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1810 (-5)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1025 (2)
CAPESIZE
A quieter start to the week with Singapore on holiday, although sentiment remains firmer following Friday’s activity. The C5TC was assessed at $40,439, up $1,044.

In the Pacific, rates strengthened with FMG fixing at $13.80 for West Australia/China on (Alpha Optimism 192,258 / 2016) ETA 20th, while there was also market talk of another major miner having covered tonnage on Friday, though this remains unconfirmed.

The Atlantic ended last week with improved sentiment and strong resistance from owners. There are indications that the market could increasingly price from northern positions, while offers on C7 have started to pull back. At the end of last week $26.75 was fixed by O&M for Saldanha Bay/Qingdao for early December dates.
PANAMAX
The week started on a stronger footing, with sentiment across both basins remaining positive and the P5TC increasing by $300 to $18,330. Trans-Atlantic demand was said to remain evident, with brokers reporting higher levels under discussion as owners maintained a firmer market view. However, market sources noted that the tonnage count, particularly off the North Continent, was beginning to increase. Fronthaul followed a similar theme, with underlying market fundamentals still said by market participants to favour further upside reflected in the levels currently being discussed.
The Guang Bo (82,245 2023) open Krishnapatnam 4 November was placed on subjects for a trip via EC South America to China, although no other information surfaced. By comparison, the Pacific saw a more subdued start to the week, with overall activity described as relatively quiet. The North Pacific was, however, said to be gaining momentum across both grain and mineral demand. Australia and Indonesia remained steadier, with some market sources highlighting a wider bid-offer spread as owners and charterers reassessed their respective positions and subsequent rate ideas.
SUPRAMAX
A slow start to the week, as expected, with the Deepavali holiday in Singapore. The 11TC average continued from last week with most routes posting negative returns, except the US Gulf, resulting in a small decline of $73 to settle at $22,873. There was little information of fixtures or rumours emanating from the East due to the holiday, but backhaul rates and the Indian Ocean remained under the most pressure, whilst South East Asia appeared flat today which may be a temporary lull. In the Atlantic positive sentiment in the North Americas continues, with an Ultramax reported in the mid $30,000’s for grains to the East Mediterrean, and the KL Somerset (63,628 2021) open Barranquilla 13-15 November rumoured fixed basis delivery Mississippi River for a trip Acajutla with grains at $34,000 to Swire. The Continent has been slower lately but scrap rates remain strong, albeit below the highs seen last month, whilst sources say the Mediterranean only needs some fresh enquiry as tonnage appears tight. The South Atlantic is said to lack nearby stems with rates gently sliding, however forward demand is more positive.
HANDYSIZE
The week opened quietly, with minimal market activity across both basins. The BHSI closed at 1,025, while the 7TC average edged up by $37 to finish at $18,455. In the Continent and Mediterranean, activity was limited and sentiment remained broadly flat, although some routes posted marginal improvements. The Princess Natali ( 39,260 2015) open Dublin fixed delivery passing Skaw via Liepaja to Algeria with grains at low $20,000's by Westerly, but further details were not disclosed. The South Atlantic was largely unchanged, while rates in the US Gulf continued to rise as fresh demand emerged. The Seastar Trojan (30,425 2010) was heard fixed from East Coast Canada to West Africa by Canpotex, while the Jiangmen Trader (37,673 2013) was fixed from SW Pass to Brazil by Pacific Basin, rate details were not disclosed for either fixture. In the Pacific, regional holidays continued to limit activity, although rates remained relatively steady despite the subdued pace.

Market Fundamentals
CISA Daily Crude Steel Production
Between 21 and 31 October, daily crude steel production at China Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills dipped 7.0% from mid-October to 1.8 Mt/day, industry association data show. Meanwhile, output stood 3.1% lower than the same period last year.

China Extends Pause on 24% Tariff on US Goods
China’s Customs Tariff Commission has extended its pause on an additional 24% tariff on US goods by two months, keeping a 10% tariff in place, Reuters reports. China will also keep special port fees on US-linked vessels suspended until 10 January 2027. The extension follows September’s Washington summit between Trump and Xi, after which both parties proposed a $60 billion package of reciprocal tariff cuts, including roughly $17 billion of US farm goods China imported in 2024, though the plan has yet to be finalised.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape saw a volatile session, with strong morning activity across the front months before prices eased during the afternoon. Nov opened at 38,250 before climbing to 38,850, with heavy morning volume around 38,750. Prices eased throughout the afternoon, with good volume around 38,500–38,550, last trading at 38,500. Dec opened at 39,000 before rallying to 39,750, with substantial morning volume at the highs, including several larger prints. Prices later weakened to 39,250,closing at that level. Q1 27 traded heavily at 29,500 before easing to 29,200–29,250 late. Q2 27 remained steady at 33,500. while Q3+Q4 27 traded at 32,750. Cal 27 saw good volume at 32,050. Overall, Cape finished off its morning highs, with Dec attracting the heaviest activity while the forward curve remained relatively steady.

PMX
PMX saw a mixed session, with early strength fading during the afternoon as Nov came under pressure while Dec remained relatively steady. Nov opened at 18,650 before climbing to 18,800, with good morning volume at the highs. Prices later weakened to 18,600,seeing a 100d print there, before last trading at 18,650. Further prompt, an operator fixed for 27/28 November at $36.75. Overall, demand stayed strong out of Brazil and West Africa for end November into the first half of December, with an auction due out of Saldanha Bay on Friday for 01/05 December dates. An operator offered some support, however, after refreshing their stem from Sept-Isles to Algeria for late November dates, and attention turned to a pair of transatlantic tenders due for auction the following day, from Brazil to Turkey for early December and from Brazil to Egypt for end November. The basin outperformed the others on Tuesday as owners rallied on a healthy injection of fresh cargoes that boosted demand. One of the transatlantic tenders, an early-December stem from Ponta da Madeira to Turkey, was fixed in the $20.00s on a Japanese-controlled vessel, which ran to around $40,000. A German operator also fixed their vessel on the Brazilian major’s early-December transatlantic cargo from Brazil to Rotterdam at $16.75, which ran to around $37,500 on a round voyage. Demand was well maintained into Wednesday after an operator bid $36.50 for their West African cargo to China, enticing ships out of the basin, while a Newcastlemax fixed out of Winning for early December in the low $35.00s. Elsewhere, an end user’s tender for a Narvik to Turkey cargo for late November fixed around the $20.00 region, which ran to around $42,500 on a voyage basis with redelivery Gibraltar. The Brazilian major returned with a cargo from Porto do Acu to Rotterdam for 07/12 December, and an operator’s vessel fixed on an end user’s cargo from Morebaya to Gijon for 24/28 November at $13.15, which ran to $47,000 with delivery Rotterdam. Additionally, an operator’s Baltimore to Kandla stem for 05/14 December fixed at $50.75, which ran to around $72,000. After the strong start to the week, a couple of transatlantic and fronthaul stems cleared some earlier tonnage on Thursday. Activity continued in the North nonetheless, as fronthaul demand stayed strong for end November and early December with a couple of fresh cargoes coming to market, while a handful of transatlantic cargoes also remained open for similar dates. Into Friday, the North saw fronthaul and transatlantic demand remain steady to end the week with for end November and early December while tonnage is stable. FIXING LEVELS ON OVERAGE LME'S OPEN SOUTH CHINA HAVE IMPROVED FROM AROUND $15-$15,500 EARLIER IN THE WEEK, TO AROUND $16,500-$17K TOWARDS THE END OF THE WEEK. NOPAC SAW HEALTHY GAINS THIS WEEK, ALTHOUGH WITH A MIXED BAG OF FIXING LEVELS REPORTED, BUT CERTAINLY IMPROVED ON THE PREVIOUS WEEK. COMING INTO THE WEEK LAST DONE LEVELS WERE AROUND $18,500-$19K BKI LEVELS AND, AFTER A SLOW START WITH LITTLE ACTIVITY, THE MARKET STARTED TO PICK UP ON TUESDAY AFTERNOON WITH RATES FOLLOWING SUIT. FIXING LEVELS HAVE IMPROVED DRASTICALLY AND WE ARE NOW SEEING A WIDE VARIETY OF FIXING LEVELS, DEPENDING ON REDELIVERY AND DATES, WITH ANYTHING FROM $19,500 TO $22K BKI BEING REPORTED AS THE WEEK COMES TO A CLOSE. AUSTRALIA WAS BY FAR THE BUSIEST SEGMENT THIS WEEK WITH PLENTIFUL FIXING AND RATES IMPROVING DRAMATICALLY OVER THE WEEK. ON MONDAY WE SAW A COUPLE OF AUSSIE ROUNDS FIXED AT MID $18'S AND $18,750 BKI RESPECTIVELY. BY TUESDAY AFTER THIS HAD ALREADY IMPROVED TO AROUND MID $19'S BKI AND AS THE WEEK ENDS WE HAVE SEEN FIXING UP AS HIGH AS $22-$22,500 BKI CJK LEVELS. HIGH FIXING VOLUMES HAVE LED TO SOMETHING OF A CLEAR OUT AS THE WEEK COMES TO AN END, PARTICULARLY EX AUSTRALIA, AND WE SEEM TO BE SEEING A SLIGHT CORRECTION ON THE FFA'S ALSO. WITH DIWALI PUBLIC HOLIDAYS IN SINGAPORE (MONDAY) AND INDIA EARLY NEXT WEEK WE EXPECT TO SEE A SLOW START TO THE WEEK AHEAD, BUT HOPEFULLY THE CURRENT MOMENTUM IS NOT LOST. The only steady performer was ECSA to WCSA, which held flat at $35,000 for Ultramaxes and $33,000 for Supramaxes US Gulf Handysize Market This week we have seen a much firmer tone in the Handysize gulf market, driven by strong cargo demand and a shortage of prompt tonnage. Fixing activity has been robust, with rates strengthening considerably compared to recent weeks. Intra-Gulf business is now commanding levels in the upper teens, while TA’s ex US Gulf have moved back over $20,000. TA business ex USEC is achieving even stronger returns. Owners are back in the driving seat, and with current fundamentals remaining supportive, the outlook for November is positive. US Gulf Supramax and Ultramax Market The active start to the week has continued and rates have started to improve. Sufficient levels of fixing have even caused a clear out the mid November positions. Inter Caribs and FH stems have re-emerged to the market so all major routes are active. Inter Caribs have settled at usd20,500 on umax, TA is back to low to mid 30's for East Med, Cont TA is sitting at around usd30k. There is still a lack of front haul grains, levels remain at mid high 20's per day. Operators are asking a premium for December dates, so the outlook is positive for the balance of this year.
